goals: Make Block Geometry Extensions geometries participate in Continuity connected-texture behavior when their canonical source or material-family semantics call for connection.
Preserve source-material identity and support applicable BGE-owned geometries consistently without duplicating BGE's canonical geometry ownership, material-family registry, or source-block mappings.
scope: Provide one centralized Fabric block-appearance bridge for Continuity rule selection without generating material- or geometry-specific CTM rules.

Consume BGE's typed canonical binding, state projection, canonical material-face semantics, and exposed surface-patch collection as the sole material and geometry authority rather than inferring families or topology from registry identifiers or Java carrier classes.

Project only explicitly equivalent canonical material state, including world-contextual vanilla snowy semantics for every canonical parent that actually carries SNOWY, while keeping geometry form, orientation, waterlogging, and unknown properties out of the canonical appearance.

Treat Continuity and the active resource pack as the sole material-rule authority by evaluating their connection predicates on BGE-projected canonical material states, then require BGE's physical patch model to prove corresponding face semantics, compatible contact planes, rendered receiver-quad bounds, and real in-plane overlap/contact.

Support full blocks, horizontal slabs, Layers, Vertical Slabs, Farmland Slab, Steps, Corners, and Quarter Columns whenever their BGE binding supplies valid surface data; leave contextual Stairs/Walls, unknown surface contracts, risky visual profiles, and unrelated Continuity behavior fail-closed or unchanged.

exclusions: Continuity remains the target CTM implementation; this project does not replace Continuity or implement a general CTM engine.

BGE retains ownership of geometry registration, geometry ownership, material-family relationships, and source-block mappings; this project must consume those canonical relationships rather than duplicate them or infer them from registry names.
Nibaru retains ownership of its material definitions and semantics.
This project does not modify BGE, Matcha, or unrelated resource-pack artwork during initialization.

Translucent Glass × BGE Compatibility remains a separate project responsible for translucent-glass and rendering compatibility issues that are not general CTM connectivity; this project does not absorb that scope.

dependencies.reason: BGE C75 owns the authoritative canonical binding, state projection, canonical material-face semantics, exposed patch geometry and typed terrain-height relation consumed generically by Canary 9; exact C75 is the controlled validation baseline.

Canary 9 decorates the exact Continuity 3.0.1+26.2 connection-predicate, processor-slice, quad-context, Standard Overlay processing/contact, and processQuadInner emission seams; required mixins and the controlled input hash fail closed on an incompatible implementation.
The appearance and block-state method descriptors are compiled and controlled against Minecraft Java 26.2.
Fabric runtime loader and required Mixin host declared by Canary 5.
Provides the Fabric block appearance, renderer quad, and controlled GameTest APIs used by Canary 5; 0.156.0+26.2 is the exact validation baseline.
Owns the Vertical Slab and Step base classes used by the centralized appearance and geometry policy; 2.0.7+26.2 is the exact controlled baseline.

state.milestone: Canary 9 separates canonical material semantics from physical BGE geometry: Continuity still owns rule selection, resource-pack predicates, connect mode, sprites, tint, layer, AO and tile selection, while its connection predicate receives BGE's canonical material states and BGE C75 surface patches exclusively govern contact, coplanarity, footprint and fail-closed topology. Standard Overlay admits authoritative partial receiver patches, and TERRAIN_HEIGHT_INSET uses the physical inset only for contact while retaining the receiver crop on the nominal exact presentation plane. Exact C8 owner evidence from the supplied C8/BGE/Continuity runtime stack is limited to three observations: full-height grass over vanilla farmland behaves correctly with the overlay suspended at 16/16 above farmland's 15/16 surface; grass beside a bottom Farmland Slab connects/overlays but C8 emits the overlay at the slab's physical 7/16 top instead of the nominal 8/16 plane; and ordinary slab side faces still do not receive the expected CTM/overlay relationship despite corresponding coplanar surfaces. No aggregate C8 result is inferred, and C9 remains runtime-untested.

exceptions.reason: The appearance bridge is compiled against the Minecraft 26.2 block-state and Fabric appearance method descriptors and must remain on the controlled target release.
regression_evidence: Canary 9 cleanly compiles and its 21/21 focused headless GameTests plus 14/14 unit tests execute against Minecraft 26.2 and Fabric API 0.156.0+26.2 with exact BGE C75.

exceptions.reason: Canary 9 injects exact Continuity 3.0.1+26.2 canonical connection-predicate, processor-slice, quad-context, StandardOverlayQuadProcessor unit-square/source-full-collision/final-contact, and processQuadInner QuadUtil.emitOverlayQuad seams; required mixins and the controlled input hash fail closed rather than guessing across an incompatible implementation.
regression_evidence: The exact Continuity 3.0.1+26.2 input is SHA-256 controlled, compiles against canonical regular/overlay connection predicates, overlay unit-square processing, quad context, source-full-collision, final Standard Overlay contact, and processQuadInner emission seams, and is verified as required client mixin targets.

current.summary: Separates Continuity-owned canonical material semantics from BGE-owned surface contact and keeps typed terrain overlays on their nominal presentation plane.
